licenses.text:
Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: Edward John Eyre (author, Wikidata Q357792), died 1901. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Eyre, Edward John, 1815-1901") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: Journals of expeditions of discovery into central Australia, and overland from Adelaide to King George's Sound, in the years 1840-1; sent by the colonists of South Australia, with the sanction and support of the government: including an account of the manners and customs of the aborigines and the state of their relations with Europeans, London, T. and W. Boone, 1845, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/journalsexpedit00eyregoog. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 92%, 86%, 86% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Edward John Eyre, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
